landmarks.name: Bratislava Castle
landmarks.writeup: A historic castle overlooking the capital city, symbolizing Slovakia's rich history and offering panoramic views.

wiki.extract: Bratislava Castle is the main castle of Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia. The massive rectangular building with four corner towers stands on an isolated rocky hill of the Little Carpathians, directly above the Danube river, in the middle of Bratislava. Because of its size and location, it has been a dominant feature of the city for centuries.

landmarks.name: Spiš Castle
landmarks.writeup: One of the largest castle sites in Central Europe, a UNESCO World Heritage site showcasing medieval architecture.

wiki.extract: The ruins of Spiš Castle in eastern Slovakia form one of the six largest castle sites in Slovakia. The castle is situated above the town of Spišské Podhradie and the village of Žehra, in the region known as Spiš. It was included in the UNESCO list of World Heritage Sites in 1993. The area of the castle is 3.9 ha. It is administered by the Spiš Museum at Levoča, a division of the Slovak National Museum.

landmarks.name: Slovak Paradise National Park
landmarks.writeup: Known for its stunning gorges, waterfalls, and hiking trails, it is a popular destination for nature lovers.

wiki.extract: Slovak Paradise National Park is one of the nine national parks in Slovakia, situated in East Slovakia. The National Park protects the area of the Slovak Paradise mountain range, which is located in the north of the Slovenské rudohorie Mountains.

landmarks.name: High Tatras
landmarks.writeup: A mountain range offering skiing, hiking, and breathtaking alpine scenery, part of the Carpathian Mountains.

wiki.extract: The High Tatras or High Tatra Mountains, are a mountain range along the border of northern Slovakia in the Prešov Region, and southern Poland in the Lesser Poland Voivodeship. They are a range of the Tatra Mountains chain.

cultural_events.name: Bratislava Music Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual classical music festival featuring international and Slovak artists.

wiki.extract: The Bratislava Music Festival is an international festival of classical music that takes place annually in the city of Bratislava, Slovakia. It is a major Slovak musical event. The festival is organised by the Slovak Philharmonic and its honorary president is Edita Gruberová.

cultural_events.name: Východná Folklore Festival
cultural_events.writeup: The oldest and largest folklore festival in Slovakia, celebrating traditional music, dance, and costumes.

wiki.extract: Východná is a village and municipality in Liptovský Mikuláš District in the Žilina Region of northern Slovakia.

food_writeup: Slovak cuisine features hearty dishes such as bryndzové halušky (potato dumplings with sheep cheese), goulash, and various meat and potato-based meals reflecting Central European influences.
brief_history: Slovakia was part of Great Moravia in the 9th century, later integrated into the Kingdom of Hungary. It became part of Czechoslovakia after World War I and peacefully separated to form an independent nation in 1993.
